assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Magnetic material
items.clue: A substance that is attracted to either pole, never repelled; iron, steel, cobalt and nickel are the ones named.

items.label: Magnetic field
items.clue: The region in which a compass needle experiences a force.

items.label: Permanent magnet
items.clue: Keeps its own field at all times, with fixed north and south poles.

items.label: Magnetic compass
items.clue: Contains a small bar that is free to turn and line up with the field.

questions.stem: The north pole of one bar magnet is brought close to the north pole of a second bar magnet. What happens to the magnets?

options.text: They repel each other, because the two poles are alike
They attract, because magnets always pull each other
Nothing happens until the two magnets are touching
They repel only if one of the magnets is stronger

questions.explanation: Two like poles repel each other, so two north poles push apart.

questions.stem: Which of these is the best definition of a magnetic field?

options.text: The set of lines drawn on a diagram around a bar magnet
The area a magnet covers when it is touching an object
The region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet
The space that fills with force once iron is placed in it

questions.explanation: The magnetic field is the region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet or on a magnetic material.

questions.stem: Two magnets on a bench push each other apart while there is still a 2 cm gap between them. Which statement best describes this force?

options.text: It is a contact force passed through the bench surface
It is a non-contact force, acting across the air gap
It is a non-contact force only while they move
It is a contact force acting through the air

questions.explanation: Attraction and repulsion between two magnetic poles are examples of non-contact force, so the force acts over a distance.

questions.stem: A magnet is held over a tray containing a copper coin, a nickel disc, an aluminium strip and a steel screw. Which objects are attracted?

options.text: All four of them, since they are all metals
The copper coin and the steel screw
Only the steel screw and nothing else
Only the nickel disc and the steel screw

questions.explanation: Nickel and steel are magnetic materials; copper and aluminium are not.

questions.stem: A steel paper clip is held near a strong magnet and becomes magnetic itself. What name is given to the paper clip while it is in the field?

options.text: The clip is a permanent magnet
The clip is a non-magnetic metal
The clip is an induced magnet
The clip is a magnetic pole

questions.explanation: An induced magnet is a material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field.

questions.stem: A bar magnet is brought near an unmagnetised iron bar. The magnet is then flipped end for end. Which statement about the force on the iron bar is correct?

options.text: It stays an attraction, whichever pole faces the bar
It now changes from an attraction to a strong repulsion
It becomes zero, because the two poles now cancel out
It stays a repulsion for each of the two poles

questions.explanation: The force between a magnet and a magnetic material is always one of attraction.

questions.stem: A chain of paper clips hangs from a bar magnet. The magnet is taken away. What happens to the paper clips?

options.text: They stay in a chain, now permanently magnetic
They push each other apart and scatter widely
They stay in a chain for the next few hours
They lose their magnetism and fall apart

questions.explanation: When removed from the magnetic field an induced magnet loses most or all of its magnetism quickly.

questions.stem: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?

options.text: In the middle of the magnet
At the poles of the magnet
Equally strong at every point
At the outer ends of the lines

questions.explanation: The field is strongest at the poles of the magnet.

questions.stem: The south pole of one bar magnet is brought near the north pole of another. Which row correctly describes the force?

options.text: Repulsion, because these two poles are different
Attraction, because unlike poles attract each other
Attraction, because south poles always attract
No force at all, as the poles are not alike

questions.explanation: Two unlike poles attract each other, and this happens for any pair of N and S poles.

questions.stem: A plotting compass is moved slowly away from the north pole of a bar magnet. What happens to the magnetic field where the compass is?

options.text: It stays exactly the same until a definite edge is reached
It gets stronger as the compass moves away from the pole
It stays the same all the way around the bar magnet
It gets weaker, because the distance from the magnet increases

questions.explanation: The strength of the magnetic field depends on the distance from the magnet, so moving away weakens it.

questions.stem: A student wants two magnets on trolleys to push apart when released. How should the magnets be arranged?

options.text: With a north pole facing a south pole
With the two magnets touching end to end
With two north poles facing each other
With one magnet turned on its side

questions.explanation: Two like poles repel each other, so N facing N gives a push apart.

questions.stem: Outside a bar magnet, which way do the magnetic field lines point?

options.text: From the north pole to the south pole
From the south pole across to the north
From each pole in towards the middle
Always straight out from each pole

questions.explanation: The direction of a magnetic field line is from the north (seeking) pole of a magnet to the south (seeking) pole.
